title: Loopback development server serves private checkout files
description: At NoctweaveJS c14aee7ad0c43c88526cbf8de5a296c5d6b7d4dd, the development static handler served all repository-contained files and followed symlinks. An actual loopback server returned HTTP200 for a synthetic0600 .local/group-companion/client-state.json. This grants listener clients access to files the server process can read, irrespective of their filesystem permissions. No arbitrary remote webpage access or protected-state decryption was demonstrated.
root_cause: Lexical containment within the whole repository was the only static file authorization check, followed by unbounded readFile with symlink following.
intended_behavior: Publish only intended browser runtime assets; private state, repository metadata and paths outside the approved asset tree must remain inaccessible.

trace.description: Requests not routed to an API reach static serving after loopback Host validation.
The decoded pathname is joined to the entire checkout root.
readFile returns private file content without an asset allowlist or symlink-target check.

evidence.description: The companion state is stored below the same root that was served publicly.
At the vulnerable ref, readFile follows links and reads any lexically contained path.
Current actual-server synthetic fixture confirms baseline HTTP200 for private state; patched server denies private paths, symlinks, non-files and oversize assets while serving legitimate assets.

conditions.description: The local browser development server is running.
Attacker can issue requests to its127.0.0.1 listener, for example another local process or OS user.
A targeted readable file exists beneath the checkout, or an asset symlink points outside it. The reproduction uses only a synthetic0600 sentinel.

execution.attacker_perspective: A client of the developer's loopback HTTP listener requests a private checkout path without filesystem access to it.
payloads: GET /client/external.js where the asset is a symlink to a synthetic outside file
instructions: Run node --test test/browser-server-security.test.js against a saved copy of the original server in the test's temporary synthetic checkout.
The fixture creates private sentinel files, two symlinks and ordinary public assets; it binds only an temporary local fixture port.
Repeat against the fixed server; do not use real user files.
execution.observed_result: Original source returnedHTTP200 for synthetic private state and failed the regression. Patched source serves four positive-control assets, denies private/encoded paths and symlink targets, rejects non-regular and oversized assets, and passes the regression. Host/SOP controls mean remote-webpage read access is not established.

remediation.strategy: Allowlist only actual browser source/assets and packaged WASM; reject hidden/traversal components and stable symlink targets; open no-follow/nonblocking, require regular files and cap reads at8MiB. Same-user concurrent ancestor renames are not claimed to be isolated by this development server.

likelihood.reason: Requires access to a running local development listener.

impact.reason: A local listener client can retrieve files readable by the developer process, including accidental plaintext secrets; protected Core state remains encrypted.

confidence.reason: Real loopback reproduction uses the Git baseline and synthetic private data; fixed positive/negative behavioral controls and independent source review passed.

title: Wrong-group admission reaches the mutating CLI before selected-group authorization
description: At NoctweaveJS c14aee7ad0c43c88526cbf8de5a296c5d6b7d4dd, an operator-selected group is checked only after group-link-add-member runs; a request for another group can therefore dispatch that group's membership mutation. The durable-Welcome recovery path can also report the selected group for a different target. The reproduction proves wrong-target CLI dispatch with a controlled stub; the real Core CLI source independently shows the request group controls the durable prepareGroupMemberAddition call. No full cryptographic membership mutation was executed in the reproduction.
root_cause: The selected group was compared with the CLI output after invocation, while the request artifact rather than the selected group determined the authoritative mutation target.
intended_behavior: Reject an admission artifact targeting any group other than the selected group before invoking a helper capable of persisting membership.

trace.description: URL-selected group and supplied requestLink are passed together to the companion.
Only UUID/text bounds were checked before writing the request file.
The group-link-add-member command runs before the result group check at line158; Core derives the mutation group from the link.

evidence.description: At the recorded vulnerable ref, the target-group comparison follows the side-effecting CLI call.
The original durable-Welcome recovery branch returns without checking the artifact target.
Current regression fixture: original source invokes the fake CLI once for a wrong group; patched source invokes it zero times. Separate recovery and duplicate-key tests cover alternate paths.

conditions.description: Victim CLI state must hold authority to admit a member in the artifact-targeted group.
Victim selects group A and supplies an attacker-controlled, otherwise valid admission link for group B.
Browser group-companion integration and native CLI are available.

execution.attacker_perspective: A prospective group member supplies a link for a different group than the operator believes is selected.
payloads: selected group A: 3f770ad9-4cea-41f0-a626-6d9e04796484; bounded admission link with version1 and groupID57364e86-d934-4f1e-9816-e18d76658bdb
instructions: Run node --test test/group-companion.test.js against the saved Git-baseline companion with its CLI replaced by the fixture stub.
The stub records invocation and returns a different group, or writes a synthetic durable Welcome then fails maintenance.
Run the same fixture against the patched companion.
execution.observed_result: Original source fails3 of7 tests: wrong-target dispatch occurs before rejection and recovery accepts a wrong-group synthetic Welcome. Patched source passes7/7 with zero CLI invocations for mismatched or ambiguous links. This is dispatch-level evidence backed by Core source trace, not a live unauthorized membership change.

remediation.strategy: Before any private-file write or CLI call, strictly decode bounded canonical base64/fatal UTF-8/duplicate-key-free JSON and bind version and group UUID to the selected group. Leave complete signature/admission validation to Core.

likelihood.reason: Requires operator interaction and authority in both relevant contexts.

impact.reason: A narrow group-admission authorization decision can be directed at the wrong group.

confidence.reason: Behavioral baseline regression, actual Core mutation source trace, and independent native-agent review agree; full cryptographic group mutation was deliberately not run.
